title: Exponential growth and decay
hook: a(1 + r)^t: the start times the growth factor, once per period.

steps.prompt: From memory: in y = a(b)^t, what do a and b mean?
steps.answer: a is the starting amount. b is the growth factor per period: above 1 is growth, between 0 and 1 is decay.

steps.prompt: A town of 5,000 grows 3% a year. Which model?
steps.why: Growth of 3% is a factor of 1.03.

steps.prompt: Drag b until y = 100 · bˣ goes through (2, 144).
steps.why: 100b² = 144, so b² = 1.44 and b = 1.2. That's 20% growth each step.

steps.prompt: A car worth $20,000 loses 15% of its value each year. The growth factor is:
Bacteria double every 4 hours, starting at 100. How many after 12 hours?

choices: The amount halves every 10 units of time
steps.why: The exponent t/10 goes up by 1 every 10 units of t, so one halving each time.

steps.prompt: $1,000 earns 4% a year. Finding the value after 2 years. Tap the line with the mistake.

steps.why: Exponential multiplies by the same factor each step (here 2). Linear adds the same amount.

keys: Model: start × (factor)^t. Growth of r%: factor 1 + r. Decay of r%: factor 1 − r.
Watch the time unit: ^(t/10) means one factor every 10 units.
Equal ratios mean exponential; equal differences mean linear.
